claims.sourceText: OSTI bibliographic record and abstract for Sasakawa, Takezawa, Sugawara and Kyotani, 'The superconducting MHD-propelled ship YAMATO-1', Proceedings of the 4th International Conference and Exhibition: World Congress on Superconductivity, volume 1, Orlando FL, 27 June to 1 July 1994, https://www.osti.gov/biblio/135352 , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE CONTROL CASE, in the principals' own words: 'In 1985 the Ship & Ocean Foundation (SOF) created a committee under the chairmanship of Mr. Yohei Sasakawa, Former President of the Ship & Ocean Foundation, and began researches into superconducting magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) ship propulsion. In 1989 SOF set to construction of a experimental ship on the basis of theoretical and experimental researches pursued until then. The experimental ship named YAMATO-1 became the world's first superconducting MHD-propelled ship on her trial runs in June 1992. This paper describes the outline of the YAMATO-1 and sea trial test results.'

claims.sourceText: Reasoning over the OSTI abstract for the YAMATO-1 paper against the opened text of US 3,322,374, https://www.osti.gov/biblio/135352 , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: Stated inference, and it is short. The propulsion mechanism US 3,322,374 claims is magnetohydrodynamic, and magnetohydrodynamic propulsion was demonstrated at sea by a civil foundation in June 1992, in public, under a named chairman, with the results reported at an international conference. THE INFERENCE IS THAT THE MECHANISM DOES NOT REQUIRE A SECRET TO EXIST and nothing more. It is not an argument about what was or was not recovered, and no edge from this node asserts one.
